# /riff — 3 variants for landing page hero

Intent: a landing page hero for a weekly briefing newsletter about small-business tech, specifically targeting SMB operators who manage multiple SaaS tools and want weekly digest content.

## Variant A — Edward Tufte (data over decoration)

Headline: "47 tools your team already uses. One briefing. 20 minutes a week."
Proof point: a 1-line sparkline showing per-week open rates for the last 12 weeks across 1,200 current subscribers.
Hero image: none. Density first.
Design rationale: Tufte's data-to-ink ratio principle applies to landing hero density. Every element earns its space. The sparkline is the only decoration; it carries data.
Typography: Charter at 18px body, 36px headline. One typeface family. One weight for prose, one for the sparkline numerals.
Color palette: ink on cream. Two accents (red for high weeks, green for recent uptick).
Preview: /tmp/riff-tufte/index.html

## Variant B — Rams (less, but better)

Headline: "The weekly briefing for people who build small things."
Proof point: one quote, one byline, white space.
Hero image: large, grayscale, single photo.
Design rationale: Rams's 10 principles — honest, unobtrusive, long-lasting. The photo carries emotional weight; the rest is scaffolding.
Typography: Helvetica Neue. 42px headline. 20px body. 15% letter-spacing on headline.
Color palette: neutral grays plus one brand color for the CTA. White space is the design.
Preview: /tmp/riff-rams/index.html

## Variant C — Walker (editorial voice)

Headline: "You read 40 tabs this week. This one is on us."
Proof point: three tags showing recent topics with hover-preview cards.
Hero image: generated collage from this week's coverage with 6-9 thumbnail tiles.
Design rationale: Walker Art Center editorial energy — hero carries curatorial point of view, not just typography.
Typography: Walker Studios typeface at 48px headline, Reader at 17px body. Two typefaces playing against each other.
Color palette: full-bleed background, dynamic per-issue.
Preview: /tmp/riff-walker/index.html

## Luminary attribution

Each variant pins a distinct lens. Picker trades off:
- Tufte — serious reader, data-first, respects attention
- Rams — minimalism signals maturity; works best for enterprise audience
- Walker — editorial energy; works best for curiosity-driven readers

Next step: pick a variant. Then say "/launch <variant>" to spec the build.
